title: Ledgerline — Instant Exports
storyboard:
# Ledgerline — Instant Exports

Length 10 seconds at 30 fps. Deliver two cuts: 16:9 (1920x1080) and 9:16 (1080x1920).

## Shot 1 (0:00–0:03) Hook
- Title reads exactly: Exports in one click
- A dark navy background with a single lime accent line drawn left to right.

## Shot 2 (0:03–0:07) Proof
- A white app card shows a table with three rows and a lime "Export CSV" button.
- A counter reads 0 at 0:03 and reads exactly 10,000 rows by 0:06.

## Shot 3 (0:07–0:10) Call to action
- Text reads exactly: Live today for every plan
- The ledgerline.app URL is visible from 0:08 to the end.
- On the 9:16 cut, nothing sits in the bottom 35% of the frame.

versions.summary:
I've written `src/Video.tsx` in one pass. I haven't rendered it or run Kane against it, so nothing below has been checked in a browser yet.

**Structure:** 10 seconds at 30 fps (300 frames) in three `<Sequence>` shots: Hook 0–90, Proof 90–210, Call to action 210–300. One component lays itself out for both 16:9 and 9:16 using `useVideoConfig()`. In the 9:16 cut, every shot's content sits inside the safe zone (below the top 14%, above the bottom 35%, 6% in from each side). That covers storyboard rule 3, which only asks for it in shot 3.

**Shot 1 – Hook:** a dark navy background with a slow-drifting faint grid and a vignette. The Ledgerline logo and wordmark sit above "Exports in one click". The title springs up and tightens its letter spacing, and a single lime line draws left to right with a glowing tip. At the end of the shot the line pulls back and the title lifts away.

**Shot 2 – Proof:** a white app card settles into place with a slight 3D tilt. It shows a "Transactions" header, a lime "Export CSV" button and a table with three rows. A cursor glides in and clicks the button, which sends out a ripple. The counter starts at "0 rows" and eases up to exactly "10,000 rows" at frame
